name: jidec-ledger
producer: JIDEC public verification ledger (HORIZON SHIELD), entries as served at GET https://ledger.horizonshield.dev/ledger/{n}?format=json
description: Scored by its operator, against this specification, from its own public source and live endpoint. Each entry carries a sequence number n, the canonical bytes of what was recorded (record_canonical), their SHA-256 (claim_sha256), and an OpenTimestamps proof that anchors that one hash to a Bitcoin block (ots_status, bitcoin_block). That is per-entry external timestamping, not a chain: no entry binds its predecessor, so an entry can be removed or the newest entries truncated and every remaining entry still verifies on its own. n is a real ordinal, so a removal in the middle leaves a visible gap, but nothing in the export states how many entries exist, so the tail is not checkable from the delivered set. The Bitcoin anchor proves that a hash existed by a block time; it does not prove the ledger delivered every hash it anchored.

integrity.note: No predecessor binding. claim_sha256 is over the entry's own record_canonical only. Each claim_sha256 is anchored individually to Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps (a per-entry external timestamp); that establishes existence by a block time per entry, and says nothing about removal or truncation of the set.

loss.note: n is assigned sequentially by the ledger worker, so a gap in n is visible to a reader. But no entry declares loss, no record states the total produced, and there is no end marker, so truncation of the newest entries is undetectable from the export alone; a reader needs an independently held latest n.

coverage.note: The ledger records what submitters and the operator's schedule send it (witness batches, specifications, datasets). It does not enumerate what it was supposed to receive; a submission that never arrived leaves no trace.

policy.note: Acceptance rules live in the worker's source, not in the entries. An entry does not bind the intake rules that admitted it.

independence.boundary_statement: The ledger is operated by the same company whose specifications, datasets and gate measurements appear in it, and the operator holds the write token. Witness batches bundle walks written by third parties, but the batch entry itself is written by the operator's worker. The Bitcoin anchor is external; the ledger is not.
